svg.title: Evaluate the analysis across simulated scenarios
svg.desc: A simulation specification defines no heat effect, a heat effect changing linearly with maternal age, and one changing nonlinearly. Acceptance criteria are set before running: bias within five grams, coverage from 92 to 98 percent, power at least 80 percent and false-positive rate no more than five percent. For each scenario, an agent repeatedly generates a dataset, runs the same prescribed analysis, and saves estimates, intervals, test results and errors. Scenario-specific true quantities reach evaluation independently of the fitting code. The comparison shows the first five saved age-28 contrast estimates and 95 percent confidence intervals against each scenario's true contrast, followed by bias, coverage, power and false-positive rates from all 400 repetitions. Muted red values and crosses mark results outside the displayed criteria. Power is evaluated under nonzero effects and false positives under no effect.
svg.text: Vary effect sizes, nonlinearities and interactions
Example: heat effects across maternal ages
First 5 of 400 repetitions per scenario; contrasts in grams
